origin: Mitchell, Keller and Kedar-Cabelli, Explanation-Based Generalization: A Unifying View, Machine Learning 1:47-80 (1986)
source_role: historical conceptual source; NOT an implementation donor or exact legacy SENS parity proof
scope: Finite acyclic Horn one-rule-per-predicate expansion over string-symbol atoms with at least one argument; an explicit operational predicate set. No negation, disjunction, effects, recursion or implicit rule preference.
behavior: Expand one symbolic goal through Horn rule heads to conjunctive operational leaves, preserving variable co-reference, constants and ordered rule-id provenance. Output is a sufficient operational clause pattern; not a minimal proof, not a learned executable opcode.
falsifiers: If parent(X,Y) and parent(Y,Z), the resulting grandparent(X,Z) precondition must preserve one shared Y, not two unbound variables
With two competing rules for a predicate, refuse rather than selecting an arbitrary explanation
With a recursive or undefined non-operational dependency, refuse rather than claiming a finite proof
If the source head contains repeated ?x, do not silently admit a target with two distinct unification variables
For all 512 possible binary parent relations on three atoms, projected operational preconditions coincide with independent relational two-step closure
